reviews.title: Misleading and Exploitative
reviews.text: You spend time watching ads, rolling limited dice, and earning food for real shelter dogs, only to discover that actually sending the food requires a minimum $9.99 monthly subscription. Treats can be sent for free, but essential food is locked behind a paywall. This wasn’t disclosed upfront. Using people’s compassion for shelter animals to push recurring subscriptions is manipulative and exploitative.

reviews.title: Glitchy and making it harder to get food
reviews.text: Every day it seems like there is a new glitch. I don’t get the rolls it is supposed to give me. And now they have decreased how many treats you get by petting your dog from 15 to 9. I feel like on some of my dogs I can never earn a health shield. They continuously make it harder to get food to these dogs and I don’t like that. I’m better off sending $6 a month to a local shelter than this game.

reviews.title: Would Love If
reviews.text: I think the concept is very cute and genuinely could be helpful, if not for a few things - my biggest concern is that you have to pay for a monthly subscription to send actual food and not just treats. If you fill both the treat and the food bar during the game they will only send the treats without a minimum $9.99 monthly fee. When/if you do choose the subscription, you get circumvented to pay through either a credit card or PayPal, not Apple Pay or the App Store (yet if you buy a few extra rolls, THAT charge IS through Apple Pay/app store). That charge? It’s sent to a foreign bank in ISRAEL. Given these issues I am extremely concerned about what data is being tracked from my phone and my payments into this app, not to mention the fee issue and a constant use of AI by the app. While I do believe that they send food to the dogs eventually, I also believe that this app is a coverup for something sketchy and am incredibly disheartened by it.

reviews.title: Charged for months for a subscription I never signed up for — support won't answer**
reviews.text:
One star, and that's generous. I found an $11.16 monthly charge from Treat App LTD on my PayPal that I never knowingly signed up for. It ran for six months — about $67 total — before I caught it. I cancelled through PayPal and emailed the company on October 16 asking for confirmation and a refund. I followed up again on October 18, in writing, and also contacted them through the app. All I got back was an automated "request received" message. No confirmation, no refund, no actual human response.

And the "game" itself? It's barely a game. You roll dice, watch ads that often don't give the rewards they promise, and then the food you "earn" costs real money to actually send. Everything funnels you toward paying. Google Play is full of reviews saying the same thing — wrong charges and support that goes silent.

Also worth knowing: the app plays up a connection to Chewy. I could not find Chewy mentioning this company anywhere. And buried in the app's own terms, they don't even guarantee the supplies reach the dog you picked.

If you're thinking of downloading this: watch your PayPal and card statements closely, because getting your money back apparently isn't part of the experience.

reviews.title: Has some improvements needed
reviews.text:
I am a person who has 3 dogs and 7 cats. I am also a disabled person and money is not easy to come by. I do like this game because it is helping other dogs and the shelters housing them.

However the game itself is tedious and a bit boring. Board game layout, roll the die and move around the board. Each tile has something to collect (albeit most are +6 “kibbles”) to help you progress and send treats to the sponsor dog.

There are mini games but I have recently found that I rarely land on the games tiles. When I do, it will be a mini game that I will have already maxed out. This makes it much harder to obtain a shield to make sure you do not lose the sponsor dog.

I did the update but the event available is for players with unlimited deliveries which is paywall number one. I get that in order to supply shelters with the items is expensive and that offering a subscription service allows for more funding but it seems that it could have been done (like many other apps) where you get basic rewards as a free player and premium rewards for people subscribed. This way no one is left out.

I have also noticed that the most recent update has seen a decline in the amount of kibble you can gain from petting the virtual pup. Prior to the update, you were able to pet the pup 5 times between each roll. This meant 15 kibbles per roll. reviews.title: Love the concept, BUT….
reviews.text: There are SO MANY glitches and bugs. One of them being that while I’m petting a dog, sometimes their health will randomly drop to 0% instead of increasing. It’s not often but often enough to cause annoyance. I reached out to support and they requested I provide screenshots but that’s not really possible as you literally cannot track when that will happen. Also, this becomes SO boring. There’s little to no variety on what players can do, it’s all chance. Rolling the dye and landing on a bone is the most useless feature. I really hate landing on those bones. Players can only send meals if they pay, treats are the only consistently free supplies we can send to dogs. If this app did not directly support shelter dogs and provide updates on their adoptions, I would have stopped using it ages ago. Please fix this.
